ABSTRACT  
Biomass - derived carbon electrode material with a porous structure is widely used in supercapacitor applica -
tions, which can improve electron transfer and shorter ion diffusion pathways. In this work, the garlic peel 
biomass carbon (GPBC), NiMo
3
S
4
(NMS) and garlic peel biomass carbon decorated with NiMo
3
S
4 
(GPBC/NMS) 
composite were prepared through a in situ two-step hydrothermal method. The synthesized materials were 
characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD) and field emission scanning electron microscopy (FE-SEM), energy 
dispersive x-ray spectroscopy (EDS), Transmission electron microscopy techniques (TEM), Raman spectroscopy 
and Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) techniques were used to analyze the structure, morphology and specific 
surface areas and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS). The prepared bimetallic metal sulfide on a biomass - 
derived carbon namely the GPBC/NMS composite is used in supercapacitor application. The GPBC/NMS com -
posite electrode exhibits good cycle performance with high specific capacity of 304C/g at current density of 1 A/ 
g in a 3 M KOH electrolyte solution. The electrochemical performance of the GPBC/NMS//GPBC asymmetric 
supercapacitor device produces an excellent energy density 45.5 Wh kg
� 1 
at a power density of 1125 W kg
� 1 
in 
the 1.6 V operating potential window. The GPBC/NMS//GPBC also exhibits 93 % retention of its initial 
capacitance after the 10,000 GCD cycle performance. The above results demonstrate a new way of developing 
high performance electrode materials for energy storage applications.   
1. Introduction 
In today's world, the consumption of fossil energy for portable 
electronic devices, electronic vehicles, and other energy-consuming 
industrialization are increasing day by day and the demand of the en -
ergy causing environmental pollution and economic issues. [ 1 , 2 ]. With 
the increase in necessity for energy, it becomes necessary to store energy 
and use it efficiently. Advanced energy storage devices such as fuel 
batteries, supercapacitors and rechargeable batteries have been suc -
cessfully relieve environmental problems and energy shortage [ 3 , 4 ]. 
Among the advanced energy storage systems, Supercapacitors are the 
main energy storage system that has attracted more attention due to 
their long cycling stability, extremely low internal resistance, high 
power density capability, fast charge-discharge cycling, and longer life 
span [ 5 ]. The supercapacitor is mainly classified into three groups ac -
cording to the energy storage mechanism: Electrode double layer ca -
pacitors (EDLC), Pseudocapacitors, and Hybrid capacitors. In recent 
years, the combination of EDLC and pseudocapacitor in the hybrid 
capacitor has attracted attention due to its high performance, good 
cycling stability, and excellent specific capacitance [ 6 – 8 ]. 
The hybrid supercapacitor is largely dependent on the nature of 
Electrodes, electrolyte, separators and current collectors. The carbon 
based electrodes such as carbon nanotube (CNT), carbon nanofiber, 
graphene, activated carbon (AC), carbon aerogel, etc. are considered to 
be the ideal electrode materials in the supercapacitor because of their 
physiochemical properties such as high chemical stability, high specific 
surface area, excellent electrical conductivity, etc. [ 9 – 11 ]. In recent 
years, biomass-derived carbon materials synthesized from various

biomasses, including banana peel [ 12 ] corncob [ 13 ], rice husk [ 14 ], 
lotus stem [ 15 ], bamboo [ 16 ], pomelo peel [ 17 ], tobacco waste [ 18 ], 
pencil peel [ 19 ] and etc., have been used as carbon sources to prepare 
carbon materials for energy storage applications. Biomass-derived car -
bon materials have the advantages of a rich carbon content, high specific 
surface area, an enlarged pore structure, and excellent electrical con -
ductivity, making them suitable for use as electrode materials in 
supercapacitor applications [ 20 – 22 ]. Utilizing biomass waste as an 
electrode sources to create abundant electroactive sites carbon with 
enhanced EDLC supercapacitor performance due to their hierarchical 
meso/micro pores and presence of various heteroatoms. To develop 
hybrid super capacitor, the effective pseudo behavior nanomaterial's are 
composed with biomass derived carbon [ 23 ]. Hybridization of transition 
metal oxides on the surface of the carbon material is enhance the elec -
trochemical performance and makes synergistic effect that takes ad -
vantages in energy storage applications. To date, high-performance 
electrodes have undergone intensive exploration and exploitation to 
meet the aforementioned demands, such as metal oxides, metal sulfides, 
metal phosphides, and so on. Specifically, transition metal sulfides 
(TMSs) have received significant attention due to their superior con -
ductivity and remarkable electrochemical performance due to their 
pseudo capacitive ability [ 24 , 25 ]. Extensive research has been carried 
out to study the high theoretical specific capacity of binary transition 
metal sulfides and their use as supercapacitor electrode materials [ 26 ]. 
Furthermore, despite its attractive electrochemical properties, the TMS 
is exhibited low specific capacity. To overcome the problem, the new 
strategy method is used to increase the specific capacitance of TMS 
materials. Due to the high charge transfer resistance and low efficiency 
of the active material, the practical specific capacity of TMS is currently 
quite low in comparison to its theoretical value [ 27 ]. In the TMS ma -
terials, NiCo
2
S
4 
is mostly examined by supercapacitors because of their 
high theoretical capacitance, low cost, and easy synthesis process. Some 
reports on NiMo
3
S
4 
battery-type materials were investigated by super -
capacitor applications [ 28 , 29 ]. Research investigations required to find 
suitable composites along with TMS for enhanced electrochemical per -
formance and redox ability through synergistic effect [ 30 , 31 ]. 
In this work, the novel NiMo
3
S
4 
embedded heteroatom doped carbon 
using natural garlic peel waste derived carbon support as support to 
enhance the conductivity of NiMo
3
S

in order to fabricate super -
capacitor. Garlic peel derived activated carbon was decorated with 
NiMo
3
S
4
(GPBC/NMS) through an in situ two-step hydrothermal process 
for energy storage applications. The GPBC was prepared by the hydro -
thermal method and activated by KOH with a developed pore structure 
to improve the conductive substrate of NMS, which could potentially 
enhance the electrochemical performance of the GPBC/NMS composite. 
In addition, the asymmetric supercapacitor assembled with GPBC/NMS 
for the positive electrode and GPBC for the negative electrode could 
produce excellent electrochemical performance. The strategy suggested 
here may inspire new possibility of sustainably producing biomass 
derived carbon materials for advanced energy storage.

2.4. Characterization method 
Various characterization techniques were used to characterize the 
synthesized materials. The crystal structure of synthesized samples was 
characterized by X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern were using Shimadzu 
XRD 6000 (Japan) instrument with Cu (k α ) radiation source and the 
scanning range of 2 θ = 10 – 80
◦
. The structure morphology of the syn -
thesized samples were examined by field emission scanning electron 
microscopy (FESEM)using a Quanta feg 250 instrument and High Res -
olution Transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM)and energy disper -
sive x-beam spectroscopy (EDS) by using a JOEL Japan, JEM-2100 plus 
instrument. Raman spectra of the samples were recorded by using a 
confocal Raman spectrometer (WITec, Germany). To analyze the 
textural properties, the nitrogen (N
2
) adsorption- desorption isotherm 
analysis was carried out at 77 K by using a Quanta Chrome Nova 2200e 
Instrument. The surface area, pore volume and the average pore diam -
eter were measured using Barrett-Joyner- Halenda (BJH) and Brunauer 
Emmett-Teller (BET) methods. The electronic state of the elements in the 
prepared composite was evaluated by X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy 
(XPS) analysis with a PHI Versaprobe III instrument.

GPBC/NMS composite and carbon black and polyvinylidene (PVDF) 
binder in a mass ratio of 80:10:10 into an N -methyl-2-pyrrolydone 
(NMP) solution to from a homogeneous slurry [ 34 ]. The slurry was 
coated on a graphite electrode (1 × 1 cm

The morphological analysis of the prepared GPBC, NMS, and GPBC/ 
NMS composite was performed by field emission scanning electron mi -
croscopy (FESEM) at various magnifications, as shown in Fig. 2 (a – i). The 
GPBC shows a flake-like shape of carbon skeleton in Fig. 2 (a – c), and the 
small sphere-shaped nanoflower-like morphology was obtained in the 
NMS as seen in Fig. 2 (d – f). From the GPBC/NMS composite, the small 
sphere-like structure of the NMS has been uniformly grown on the 
irregular-like shape of the carbon surface, as shown in Fig. 2 (i-k). The 
morphology of the synthesized materials was confirmed by transmission 
electron microscopy (TEM) analysis exhibited in Fig. 3 . The GPBC shows 
nanosheet like structure and the NMS exhibits a block shade crystal like 
structure. The NMS material of crystal structure wrapped on the sheet 
like structure of GPBC material and the Selected Area Electron Diffrac -
tion (SAED) pattern of GPBC and NMS shows amorphous and crystalline 
nature respectively. SAED pattern of GPBC/NMS composite exhibits 
both amorphous and crystalline nature and this result reveals the con -
firms the composite formation ( Fig. 3 ) [ 41 ]. 
The EDS analysis carried out on the composite material shows the 
presence of Carbon (C), Nickel (Ni), Molybdenum (Mo) and sulfur (S) 
elements. There were no other elements observed in the EDS analysis 
and their atomic percentages are shown in Fig. S1 (a & b) and Table 1.
